conclusion: ShriSingajiMalwa's near-plant soundings are entirely from one month (January), while its background ring also draws from April/May (mean XCO2 ~415.6-416.5 ppm) and October -- months with no near-plant coverage at all, likely due to OCO-3 swath geometry only crossing the tight near-plant circle on some overpasses. This means the original near-minus-background comparison was implicitly comparing January (near) against a January/April/May/October blend (background), and April/May's regional CO2 baseline is genuinely ~3.5-4.5 ppm higher than January's for reasons unrelated to the plant (seasonal atmospheric cycle). Restricting the comparison to the one month both zones actually share (January) flips the sign: near=412.321 vs bg=412.029 ppm, a difference of +0.292 ppm (z=2.13) -- small and only marginally significant, but positive, consistent with a real (weak) plant signal rather than the -1.052 ppm 'negative enhancement' that was actually a seasonal-sampling-imbalance artifact. This resolves the anomaly: it was not a real negative CO2 signal, a pipeline bug, or evidence against the plant emitting -- it was two systematically different seasons being averaged together and compared as if they were the same background. physics_gaussian.py's IME calculation does not currently stratify near/background comparisons by month, so this failure mode could in principle recur for any facility with uneven near/background month coverage, not just this one.
